ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOS against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the South African Targeted Financial Sanctions List published by the FIC, and Interpol-noted red flags. Accountable institutions under FICA must apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs. Standard cross-border compliance practice for USD rails also mandates screening against the OFAC SDN List and EU Consolidated List, despite not being a domestic South African statutory obligation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services Portal (Corporations and Intellectual Property Commission, South Africa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name must be in any of the 11 South African official languages; names in Latin script only. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. Names may include a registered translation in any official language. The name must not be offensive, misleading, or imply any connection with the state, a regulatory body, or a person without consent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name reservation generates a CIPC rejection notice. The applicant may submit a Request for Name Reconsideration to CIPC within 60 days. If unresolved, an appeal may be lodged with the Companies Tribunal under s.160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008, accompanied by the prescribed filing fee. No extension is available; a lapsed reservation requires a fresh name reservation application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may serve as the registered office for correspondence and service of process; however, for a Class III medical device manufacturer, a physical production, sterilization, and warehousing facility is mandatory. The registered office address must be located in South Africa and accessible to the public during business hours.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 80% risk of unannounced on-site inspections after SAHPRA licensing for Class III MedTech manufacturing. CIPC does not typically inspect registered offices during incorporation, but the Department of Employment and Labour and SAHPRA conduct operational inspections with limited prior notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) with Memorandum of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares issued at par value determined in Memorandum of Incorporation; funds must be held in a South African bank account pending confirmation of allotment

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Obtain Name Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File CoR 9.1 application for name reservation specifying the proposed name 'ZA Coronary Stent (Pty) Ltd'. Submit no less than two alternate names. Pay prescribed fee via CIPC eFiling. Await biographic screening against existing trademarks and close corporations. Upon approval, obtain name reservation certificate valid for 6 months.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is refused, file a formal objection or a follow-up CoR 9.1 with new alternate names; CIPC provides a 20-day appeal period before the Companies Tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Submit Incorporation Documents to CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) – eFiling Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) and attach the Memorandum of Incorporation setting out capital structure, director powers, and registered office address. Notarize director consents (CoR 14.2) and confirm initial directors. Pay filing fee via electronic transfer. Upload all signed documents in PDF format with embedded signatures.
required_dossiers: Certified ID / passport copies of directors
Proof of registered office address (lease or ownership deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a query or deferral, rectify the cited deficiencies within 10 business days by filing a corrected CoR 14.1 via the same portal; request expedited review if correction is trivial.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Incorporation Certificate and Company Registration Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After CIPC approval, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation (CoR 14.3) from the CIPC eFiling dashboard. Verify that the registration number (e.g., 2025/XXXXXX/07) is correctly reflected. Ensure the company is entered into the Companies Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a request for rectification of the registration record with CIPC; provide supporting affidavits if the certificate contains any typographical errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene First Board Meeting and Adopt Governance Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board (internal corporate action, notarized by company secretary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Call the first board meeting in accordance with the Memorandum of Incorporation. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution confirming share subscription, registered office, and officer appointments. Record in written minutes, have each director sign, and retain the resolution book at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director is unavailable, use written consent resolution in lieu of a physical meeting; ensure all required authorizations are obtained within 7 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Income Tax, VAT, and Payroll Taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the SARS registration via eFiling using the issued company registration number. Register for Corporate Income Tax (CIT), VAT (if annual turnover exceeds the mandatory threshold), and Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE). Submit supporting incorporation documents. Obtain a tax compliance status pin and letter of good standing.
required_dossiers: Financial institution confirmation of share capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS rejects or delays registration, file a request for reconsideration with supporting documents; escalate via the SARS branch office if no response in 15 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register as Employer and Open Operational Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SARS and a regulated South African commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File EMP-101 with SARS to register as an employer. Open a corporate bank operating account with a commercial bank; provide the bank with certified company documents, tax clearance letter, and board resolution designating authorized signatories. Activate Swift wire and Letter of Credit facilities for international trade.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional beneficial ownership information, complete the relevant FIC forms and resubmit; appeal to the bank's compliance officer if the application is declined.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodge Initial Annual Return and Securities Registry Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the first 60 days post-incorporation, file the initial annual return (CoR 30.1) and establish a securities register in accordance with the Companies Act. Record all issued shares, shareholders, directors, and company secretary details in the registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If late filing penalties apply, submit a condonation application under CIPC practice notes and pay the prescribed late fee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: South African Health Products Regulatory Authority (SAHPRA) in coordination with the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (dtic) Licensing Division

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) – Environmental Impact Assessment Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report (Category A) due to laser micro-machining operations, solvent use, and potential toxic waste generation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with National Water Act (Act 36 of 1998) effluent limits: pH 6-9, biochemical oxygen demand ≤ 10 mg/L, total suspended solids ≤ 25 mg/L, and VOC emissions limited to 20 mg/m3 per stack in accordance with National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act (Act 39 of 2004). Hazardous waste must be disposed through licensed contractors under South African Waste Bureau criteria.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the local Fire and Rescue Services after inspection; structural load examination certificate from a registered professional engineer for cleanroom floors and equipment mounts; and occupational health and safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (Act 85 of 1993) including chemical hygiene, laser safety, and protective equipment verification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS), portal: SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za); customs declaration processing through SARS Customs Connect/eCANCOR.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the (Pty) Ltd with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; CIPC data transfer to SARS automatically generates the provisional income tax reference number (ITR). 2) Appoint a Public Officer within one month under s246 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011. 3) Register for VAT via form VAT101 within 21 days of taxable turnover exceeding ZAR 1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary registration is available once turnover exceeds ZAR 50,000. 4) Register for PAYE/SDL/UIF (EMP101) where employees are engaged. 5) Register as a SARS customs client to obtain an exporter code before submitting SAD500 export declarations. 6) Non-resident parent or service entities must apply through the TRS (Tax Registration Status) process to obtain a non-resident tax reference number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a South African tax-resident (Pty) Ltd is subject to corporate income tax at 27% on worldwide income, capital gains tax at an 80% inclusion rate, and 20% dividends tax on distributions; no pass-through classification is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no check-the-box regime. Applicable elections include: VAT group registration (s50 of the VAT Act 89 of 1991); voluntary VAT registration (s23 VAT Act); input-tax de minimis apportionment under s17(1) VAT Act; controlled-foreign-company elections under s9D Income Tax Act; hybrid mismatch elections under s25H and interest limitation elections under s23M; and Research & Development allowance elections under s11D Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: ZAR 1,000,000 taxable turnover in any consecutive 12-month period (s23(1) VAT Act). Voluntary registration: ZAR 50,000 (s23(2) VAT Act). Non-resident vendors with a South African economic presence are likewise registrable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping is currently in force. Tax invoices must satisfy s20 VAT Act requirements and may be issued electronically provided the data is preserved intact and legible for at least five years. VAT returns (VAT201) are filed electronically through eFiling; customs export clearance is fully electronic via SARS Customs with SAD500 submission and release. SARS is developing e-invoicing interoperability, but no API-based real-time invoice authorization applies as of the current tax year.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under s11(1)(a) VAT Act where the vendor exports movable goods, including Class III drug-eluting coronary stents manufactured under ISIC 3250, within 90 days of the date of the tax invoice (or an extended period approved by SARS not exceeding 12 months), title passes to the non-resident buyer offshore, and the vendor retains documentary proof of export. Offshore services supplied to non-residents may qualify under s11(2)(l) where the beneficiary is outside South Africa at the time of supply, the services are not consumed in South Africa, and no direct connection exists to South African immovable or movable property.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) evidencing movement of goods out of South Africa
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or SWIFT MT103 credit evidencing receipt of foreign currency export proceeds
Full tax invoice complying with s20 VAT Act
SAHPRA export clearance or certificate for the Class III stents, where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS applies post-export refund integrity audits. Failure to export within the 90-day period or absence of valid documentation triggers a deemed standard-rated supply under s10(23) VAT Act, clawing back the zero rating at 15% output VAT with statutory interest. Understatement penalties under TAA ss221-223 range from 10% (standard) to 150% (intentional evasion) of the tax shortfall, potentially up to 200% for undisclosed reportable arrangements. Criminal prosecution for fraudulent export zero-rating can result in fines and/or imprisonment of up to five years (TAA s235), restitution orders, and revocation of the SARS exporter code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) — Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) administering the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933, the Exchange Control Regulations, and the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers; licensed commercial banks act as Authorised Dealers (ADs) under Section 9A of the Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The ZAR is a floating currency. Current-account transactions are fully convertible and may be settled freely through an Authorised Dealer with supporting documentation. Capital-account transactions remain subject to exchange-control surveillance, with inward direct investment (equity or shareholder loans) permitted without prior SARB approval but requiring AD registration via Form A and inward-transfer notification. Profit remittances (dividends) are permitted provided the AD receives an auditor-confirmed dividend resolution, a SARS tax-compliance status, and Foreign Investment/Portfolio Investment forms where applicable. Capital repatriation on liquidation requires proof of the original inflow and a FinSurv-approved disinvestment certificate. Non-resident ownership of a (Pty) Ltd is permitted, and there are no residuary restrictions on foreign shareholding percentages, subject only to FICA-driven source-of-funds verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must repatriate 100% of invoice value to South Africa within 180 calendar days from the date of shipment (extendable to 360 days with AD/FinSurv approval). The historical mandatory conversion of export proceeds into ZAR was abolished effective 1 January 2021; an exporter may now retain proceeds in a domestic Foreign Currency Account (FCA) or convert to ZAR at its discretion. Failure to timeously receive export proceeds exposes the exporter to administrative penalties under the Exchange Control Regulations (typically 0.5% per month of the outstanding sum) and may trigger suspension of the exporter's FCA facility.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium. Offshore Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) do not hold a South African banking licence or Authorised Dealer status and therefore cannot open ZAR-denominated accounts, issue resident bank guarantees, or settle through the South African Multiple Option Settlement (SAMOS) system. EMIs may only operate via licensed AD partnerships for cross-border payments. For a Class III coronary-stent manufacturer, EMIs are impractical for capital escrow, letter-of-credit issuance, statutory export repatriation, or FEC hedging; their permissible use is limited to low-value operational expenditures. Onboarding such an entity through an EMI would additionally trigger FICA enhanced due diligence without conferring regulated-deposit protection.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid regime. The Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA) requires verification of identity, residential/business address, and source of funds for all directors, signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs). In practice, at least one director or UBO must attend an in-person interview at the AD's corporate banking branch; Standard Bank, FNB, and Absa permit hybrid remote onboarding with authenticated video interviews, biometric checks, and notarised/apostilled documents for lower-risk profiles. A foreign-owned, high-risk MedTech manufacturer will, however, trigger enhanced due diligence, typically requiring a physical board interview, an on-site visit, and a compliance sign-off from the bank's Governance, Risk and Compliance committee before transactional limits are activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign UBO structure with non-resident shareholder depositing lump-sum capital without traceable history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified source-of-wealth statement; 12-month original bank statements of the investing shareholder; audited financial statements of the investing entity; certificate of incorporation and register of directors; SARS tax clearance; notarized share-subscription or loan agreement; UBO organisational chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Class III medical-device designation triggering health-sector and export-control scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAHPRA establishment and product licences; ISO 13485:2016 certificate; audited financials; definitive counterparty list with banking references; sample purchase orders and pro-forma invoices; SARS customs code registration; import/export compliance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large upfront capital injection disproportionate to early-stage operating revenues
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized board resolution approving the funding; executed shareholder agreement with repayment/dividend covenants; detailed board-approved treasury and capex deployment plan; confirmation that remittances originate from the shareholder's own account; AD inward-transfer acknowledgment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex group ownership (offshore holdco with intermediate tiers) obscuring beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group-wide organisational chart; certificates of good standing for all intermediate entities; registers of directors and shareholders; Memorandum of Incorporation of the ZA (Pty) Ltd; tax residence certificates for each entity; group transfer-pricing policy governing intercompany funding and IP licence flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering screening on high-value stent component exports to third-party distributors in multiple jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices, packing lists, airway bills or bills of lading; insurance certificates; transfer-pricing documentation for related-party distribution; product-cost breakdowns; annual independent review of export transactions; end-user certificates where required by export regulations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity or shareholder-loan transfers must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 to the company's USD FCA or ZAR operational account at the appointed Authorised Dealer. The payment must carry a purpose code denoting inward direct investment ('Equity Capital Contribution' or 'Shareholder Loan'), and the AD must receive a Form A / inward-transfer notification simultaneously. The AD verifies the source of funds, issues a unique inward-transfer reference, and records the transaction in the SARB Financial Surveillance system. Equity inflows above the applicable voluntary-notification threshold require FinSurv designation; net proceeds are to be held in the Capital Escrow Account until share certificates and the updated CIPC securities register are produced. The escrow release protocol also requires a SARS tax-compliance statement and, where the shareholder is a foreign entity, a certificate of residence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments; MT700/MT701 for import Documentary Letters of Credit covering raw-material procurement (cobalt-chromium alloys, polymer coatings, laser micro-machining consumables); MT760 for standby LCs securing performance guarantees and advance-payment bonds; MT202 for interbank cover in ZAR settled via the SAMOS real-time gross settlement system. All outbound disbursements require source documents (commercial invoice, customs entry, transport evidence, and — for related parties — transfer-pricing support). The AD monitors each transaction and reports cross-border ZAR flows to FinSurv on a T+1 basis.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward Exchange Contracts (FECs) booked with an Authorised Dealer for firm USD/ZAR commitments, typically up to 12 months and renewable
Currency options on USD/ZAR executed OTC through the AD or listed on the JSE
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) approved by FinSurv where the notional exposure or tenor exceeds the AD's discretionary limits
Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing USD/ZAR, permissible for non-resident counterparties and where onshore FEC cover is unavailable
USD/ZAR futures on the JSE for short-dated, centrally cleared inventory and receivables hedging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 30 business days after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties escalate from ZAR 100 for the first 30 days of default to a maximum of ZAR 1,000 after 180 days; persistent non-filing can lead to administrative deregistration and strike-off under section 82 of the Companies Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Register Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted together with the Annual Return; beneficial ownership changes arising from shareholding transfers must be filed within 10 business days after the company receives the required notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain beneficial ownership information may expose the company and each defaulting director to administrative penalties of up to ZAR 1 million under the General Laws Amendment Act 22 of 2022.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required for public and state-owned companies; a private Pty Ltd company is also required to have its annual financial statements audited when its Public Interest Score is 350 or more for the relevant financial year. A company below this threshold is generally exempt from compulsory audit unless its memorandum of incorporation, shareholders, or a regulator requires an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or IFRS for SMEs as adopted in South Africa, depending on the size and Public Interest Score of the company; annual financial statements must be prepared within six months after the financial year-end.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a register of beneficial owners at its registered office and confirm the identity, percentage holding, and nature of control of every beneficial owner with CIPC as part of the annual return. Any shareholding transfer altering beneficial ownership must be reflected promptly in the statutory registers and reported to CIPC within 10 business days of the company being notified of the change.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for all companies and close corporations (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; 28% for earlier years).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday; the effective rate is reduced by: (i) section 11D R&D allowance (150% deduction of qualifying R&D expenditure, subject to DSI pre-approval); (ii) section 12C accelerated capital allowance on manufacturing plant and machinery (40% in year 1 and 20% per annum thereafter); (iii) section 12H learnership allowance; (iv) small business corporation (SBC) preferential rates of 0%, 7% and 21% for qualifying companies with turnover under ZAR 20 million.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carry-forward of assessed losses under section 20 of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962; the quantum available is restricted under section 20A where more than 50% of shares change ownership and the same trade is not carried on within a one-year window).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return) filed via the SARS eFiling portal (https://efiling.sars.gov.za); mandatory electronic filing for all companies; supporting annual financial statements, tax computation schedule and transfer-pricing declarations are attached.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year (e.g., a 31 March year-end return is due no later than 31 March of the following calendar year); SARS may shorten this period by public notice for a class of taxpayers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SARS tax reference number, company registration number (e.g., 2023/123456/07), trading name and registered address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only the South African resident entity's identifiers; foreign parent details are captured in the shareholder/beneficial-owner declaration schedules, not in the identity fields.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the 12-month year of assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the period with the South African company's financial statements; non-resident parent reporting periods are irrelevant for this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income including domestic and export sales of coronary drug-eluting stents, licensing fees and all South African-source receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only South African-source gross income under section 9(2) of the Income Tax Act; foreign dividend or CFC inclusions must be disclosed separately in the CFC schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income exempt under section 10(1), e.g., exempt local dividends and qualifying foreign dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim exemption for dividends not meeting the participation and round-tripping requirements; attach the section 10(1)(k) holding analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, operating expenses, section 12C capital allowances, section 11D R&D deductions and other chapter II deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany charges (royalties, management fees, purchases from overseas affiliates) must be at arm's length; state in the TP schedule and cap deductions to the arm's-length amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Section C – Box 6 (Assessed loss brought forward)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year assessed loss available for set-off; subject to trade continuity and section 20A shareholding-change restrictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses of the South African tax entity are allowed; losses cannot be imported from a foreign group member under section 20(2).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Section D – Box 7 (Taxable capital gain)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Inclusion of 80% of net capital gain or the assessed capital loss brought forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company is taxed on capital gains only from immovable property in South Africa or assets of a South African permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Section E – Box 8 (Taxable income and normal tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income = gross income less exempt income less allowable deductions plus taxable capital gain; normal tax at 27% before rebates and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are capped at the South African tax on the same foreign-source income; attach the foreign tax credit reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Section E – Box 9 (Dividend and withholding tax declarations)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of dividends paid during the year and dividend tax (20%) withheld and remitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For dividends paid to a foreign shareholder, attach the DTE declaration, shareholding period and the shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate supporting treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration by the representative taxpayer (CEO/CFO/director) that the return is true and complete, together with the auditor's or accounting officer's details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The South African director signing the declaration assumes personal criminal liability for false statements under section 235 of the Tax Administration Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative non-compliance penalty (ANCP) of up to ZAR 16,500 per month under sections 210-213 TAA until the return is filed; late payment: 10% unremitted penalty plus prescribed-rate interest (sections 187/190 TAA); understatement penalties of 0% to 200% of the tax shortfall under sections 222-223 TAA; estimated assessments and criminal prosecution for wilful non-compliance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IRP6 (Provisional Tax Return) filed via SARS eFiling by every provisional taxpayer, including all companies; payments are made by electronic funds transfer or through SARS payment channels.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Semiannual (mandatory first and second provisional payments at the end of the 6th and 12th months of the year of assessment; a voluntary third 'top-up' payment may be made within 6 months after year-end).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: First provisional: within 6 months of the start of the year of assessment. Second provisional: on or before the last day of the company's year of assessment. Third provisional (optional): within 6 months after year-end to reduce interest exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated total taxable income for the current year and 50% of the estimated normal tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The estimate must be a bona fide projection; the first payment must be at least 50% of the prior year's 'basic amount' to avoid under-payment exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revised estimate of actual taxable income; cumulative payments must reach 90% of the actual liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Underestimation by more than 10% triggers a 20% estimation penalty under section 163 TAA; align with the final ITR14 figures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Optional additional payment to settle 100% of the actual tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the top-up to avoid further interest; non-resident groups frequently top up after finalising group consolidations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: IRP6 – Section 4 (Attributable dividend and CFC income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Inclusion of distributions and attributable CFC income in the estimate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CFC passive income inclusions under section 9D must be reflected in both provisional and annual returns.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 20% underestimation penalty (section 163 TAA) where the second provisional estimate is less than 90% of actual taxable income; prescribed-rate interest on outstanding provisional tax; ANCP for non-submission of IRP6 of up to ZAR 16,500 per month; a 10% unremitted-penalty regime applies to late provisional payments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% Dividend Tax under sections 64EA-64N of the Income Tax Act; the South African company declaring the dividend must withhold 20% from the beneficial owner's payment and remit it to SARS within 30 days of the dividend declaration or payment, whichever is earlier.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To reduce the 20% statutory rate under a double tax agreement (DTA), the foreign beneficial owner must: (i) submit a DTE declaration-and-undertaking (SARS form DTE-001) to the paying company or SARS before the dividend is paid; (ii) provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its country of residence; (iii) satisfy the DTA's beneficial-ownership and 18-month minimum shareholding test (unless the treaty prescribes a different holding period); (iv) retain evidence that the shares are held for the shareholder's own benefit. The reduced rate is generally applied at source; where the full 20% was withheld, the shareholder may claim a refund via the IT8WS form. The DTE number must be evidenced in the ITR14 dividend schedule.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest WHT: statutory 15% under sections 50A-50H on interest paid to a foreign person (exemption for listed tradable debt and domestic debt); DTA rates: 0% (US, UK, Germany with conditions) to 10% (Netherlands, Belgium, corporate interest). Royalty WHT: statutory 15% under sections 49A-49H on IP royalties; DTA rates: 10% under most South African DTAs (e.g., UK, Netherlands) and 12% under the US treaty. Treaty relief requires the same TRC and beneficial-ownership protocol as dividends, filed on the applicable DTE forms before remittance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File are mandatory when the aggregate value of 'affected transactions' (cross-border transactions with connected persons) exceeds ZAR 50 million in a year of assessment, or when the company's gross receipts or turnover exceeds ZAR 100 million. A Country-by-Country (CbC) Report is required where the consolidated group revenue is at least ZAR 10 billion. SARS may call for TP documentation below these thresholds under sections 29/30 TAA and section 31 of the Income Tax Act.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa has no separate ESR statute, but economic substance is embedded in the Controlled Foreign Company (CFC) rules (section 9D), the Foreign Business Establishment (FBE) exemption, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR, sections 80A-80L) and the section 103(1) anti-avoidance provisions. A taxpayer claiming treaty benefits or CFC relief must prove substantive activity: local premises, personnel, equipment, operational management, demonstrated risk-taking and genuine income-generating activities. For a Class III medical device manufacturer, the SAHPRA manufacturing licence, sterile manufacturing plant, R&D laboratory and registered pharmaceutical establishment are the core substance evidence; a 'letterbox' or conduit entity holding only IP and contracts with no local plant, qualified staff or regulatory licence will be recharacterised: interest and royalty deductions denied, CFC income imputed at 27%, dividends treated as deemed distributions, and the arrangement consolidated into a single taxpayer under section 80B.
